title: Response cache forges http.Response.Proto to HTTP/1.1 and drops every header except Content-Type on 2xx GETs
reasoning: Found by PROTO-010 (docs/investigation/PROTO-010-http2-http3-client.md). pkg/client/cache.go:110-126 - the cache round-tripper rewrites Proto to HTTP/1.1 and discards all response headers except Content-Type for cached 2xx GETs. Consequences: (1) any caller reading Proto to learn the negotiated protocol is lied to, which is exactly the signal PROTO-017 must rely on; (2) every header-based consumer (retry-after, etag, cache-control, content-encoding, rate-limit headers) silently sees an empty set on a cache hit, so behaviour differs between a miss and a hit for the same resource. Not a caching design choice - it is header loss. Fix must preserve the cache and keep the true Proto; a test must prove miss and hit return the same Proto and the same header set.

title: FIX: the CLI drops WebDAV verb request bodies - `internal/builtin/request.go` attaches a body only for POST/PUT/PATCH, so a PROPFIND sends none and the whole-webdav-for-muster goal cannot work
reasoning: FILED BY THE RELEASE DRIVER. PROTO-015's REMAINING named this as the CLI dropping WebDAV verb bodies and pointed at specs/PROTOCOLS.md order 11 / matrix row 17 as the 'owner'; the driver then checked both boards and found NO ROW anywhere that fixes it. PROTO-010 section 8 documented the defect, PROTO-015 recorded it, and demo 20 asserts the broken behaviour (body_len=0 for PROPFIND) - so the state is fully known and completely unowned. Documenting a defect in a spec is not the same as filing it, and order 11 of a matrix does not dispatch a worker. WHY IT IS RELEASE-SCOPE, not a nice-to-have: the goal for this release includes having WebDAV 'support muster' - Muster acting as a CLIENT of bunkerd's WebDAV surface. A WebDAV PROPFIND carries a body (the property request); if the client drops it, Muster cannot ask for props, which is most of what WebDAV is for. The transports (PROTO-014 h2, PROTO-015 h3) are in place and cannot help: this is the layer above them. THE FIX: `internal/builtin/request.go` attaches a body only for POST/PUT/PATCH. WebDAV verbs (PROPFIND, PROPPATCH, REPORT, MKCOL, LOCK, SEARCH) are none of those. Attach the body whenever the caller supplies one, or when the method is one that can legally carry a body - RFC 9110 permits a body on any method, so an allow-list is the wrong shape and has to be replaced rather than extended. PROOF REQUIRED: a test that issues a PROPFIND WITH a body and asserts the server received it (R2), plus inverting demo 20's body_len=0 assertion. Do not simply delete the assertion - it currently records the bug, so it must be turned into the proof of the fix. MUSTER CONVENTIONS: CGO_ENABLED=1; use `go test -short ./...` (a bare `go test ./...` runs a 30-minute soak that panics on the 10-minute per-package timeout and looks like your failure); commit gate `gitreins guard` - note core.hooksPath points at a .githooks directory that does not exist, so no hook fires and you must run the guard BY HAND and report it verbatim; `./demo/run-all.sh` is the real e2e gate but needs a .venv on PATH (the demo services are Python).

title: Caller-context propagation middleware: a proxy must forward the client-declared deadline/budget down the chain so every layer is aware and timeouts align BY DEFAULT - not by each service's private constant
source: Bane 2026-10-03 (TR-243 follow-up): 'think about and add tasks for the service we have muster around proxying and pushing down values that the client is using so the proxy layers forward it and are aware and the server can therefore be aware and have aligned timeouts by default'
reasoning:
Muster already owns the proxy seam (pkg/daemon ProxyServer, pkg/client, internal/middleware) and specs/PROTOCOLS.md is the design authority for protocol and transport work, so the propagation contract belongs here as a first-class feature rather than as a convention each consumer re-implements.

CONTRACT - caller-declared tolerance, propagated hop by hop.

Measured defect (2026-10-03, the TR-160 flip): three layers each held their own
undisclosed time budget and the SHORTEST silently won.
  scheduler: gateway_response_timeout = 30m, mode=idle   (the caller)
  proxy:     buffered hop = 180s wall / idle 1800s        (the middle)  <- binding
  gateway:   provider outbound 90s-600s per provider      (the server)
Result: 47 of 98 proxied requests died at exactly 180.08s (hop-wall-timeout,
task_label "timed out") while the requests that WERE served took a median 139s and
up to 426s - the middle layer was killing turns that were about to answer.

REQUEST headers (caller -> every layer):
  X-Caller-Name          who is asking (the router already reads x-router-caller)
  X-Caller-Budget-S      total seconds the caller will wait for the FINAL answer,
                         measured from request start
  X-Caller-Deadline-Mode idle | wall  (idle = the caller's timer resets on real
                         upstream progress; wall = it does not)
  X-Caller-Idle-Budget-S max tolerable SILENCE when mode=idle
  X-Caller-Max-Hops      attempts the caller will pay for (router already reads
                         x-router-max-hops)
  X-Caller-Margin-S      housekeeping the caller needs back after the response

RESPONSE headers (layer -> caller), the APPLIED values:
  X-Applied-Layer, X-Applied-Budget-S, X-Applied-Deadline-Mode,
  X-Applied-Hop-Budget-S, X-Applied-Declared (true|false)
  X-Applied-Stricter-Than-Caller   present ONLY when this layer had to be stricter,
                                   carrying the reason

RULES:
  1 READ the declared values and use them as this request's defaults. Absent -> fall
    back to configured defaults AND stamp declared=false on the row and on the
    response, so the guess is VISIBLE rather than silent.
  2 NEVER be silently stricter. A layer may be stricter only when its transport
    cannot support the declared budget, and it must say so in the response AND the
    ledger.
  3 SUBTRACT and FORWARD: forward X-Caller-Budget-S minus this hop's elapsed time and
    this layer's margin. Never forward the original unchanged - that re-inflates the
    budget downstream and undoes the whole contract.
  4 ECHO the applied values so the caller can assert alignment in the SAME round trip.
  5 RECORD on every row:
      deadline: {declared_s, mode, applied_s, layer, aligned, stricter_reason}
    so "which layer is the narrowest link" is a query, not a log grep.
detail:
Deliverable: one middleware that (a) parses the caller-context headers, (b) sets its own budget from the declared values rather than a private default, (c) forwards the value decremented by elapsed time and its own margin, (d) echoes the applied values, and (e) records the alignment decision. Any service fronted by a Muster proxy then inherits aligned timeouts by DEFAULT, which is the point.

Spec first: add the contract to specs/ (cross-reference specs/PROTOCOLS.md, which already governs the protocol/transport seam), then implement in pkg/daemon + pkg/client + internal/middleware, then prove it in the demo gate (./demo/run-all.sh is the real e2e gate; make demo is partial).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. A spec under specs/ (cross-referencing specs/PROTOCOLS.md, the design authority for the protocol/transport seam) defines the caller-context headers, the derive/forward/echo rules, and the NEVER-SILENTLY-STRICTER invariant.
2. Middleware in internal/middleware, wired into pkg/daemon ProxyServer, parses the caller context and sets the proxy's own budget FROM it rather than from a private constant - unit + integration tests.
3. The forwarded value is DECREMENTED by this hop's elapsed time plus the layer's margin; a test captures the downstream request headers and an unchanged passthrough FAILS.
4. The response echoes the applied values (layer, budget_s, mode, hop_budget_s) so a caller can assert alignment in the same round trip.
5. pkg/client exposes the SENDER side so any Muster-backed client declares its tolerance rather than defaulting silently.
6. ./demo/run-all.sh (the real e2e gate) proves the flow with TWO chained proxies, showing the budget decrement hop by hop and the alignment record.
7. A conformance test asserts, for a declared budget the legacy default would have violated, that every layer's applied budget >= declared - margin and that the total chain time stays inside the declared budget.
8. A service fronted by a Muster proxy gets aligned timeouts with NO per-service constant configured - that is the "by default" claim and it needs its own test.

CROSS-PROJECT DEPENDENCY (not a board id, kept out of depends_on because boardctl validates depends_on against THIS board): the caller side of this contract is the scheduler's SCHED-GAP-1724, the middle layer is task-router TR-264, and the server leg is task-router TR-266.

title: P1: SOAP adapter envelope is not namespace-qualified — every real WSDL 1.1 service with a targetNamespace rejects muster's call with 'Invalid namespace' — PROTO-008 fails live end-to-end
description: Dogfood 2026-10-10 (run 14) against a live public SOAP service. `openapi-cli protocol soap --wsdl /tmp/numconv.wsdl --operation NumberConversion-NumberToWords --args '{"ubiNum":1234567}'` fails: `INTERNAL_ERROR: soap: Error processing request: Invalid namespace '' expected 'http://www.dataaccess.com/webservicesserver/'`. The generated envelope (via --document) is `<soapenv:Body><NumberToWords><ubiNum>...</ubiNum></NumberToWords></soapenv:Body>` — the payload element carries NO namespace, so every document/literal service whose input element is namespace-qualified (the norm; spec §2.1 maps `<definitions targetNamespace>` to the document namespace) rejects it. Control experiment: identical envelope hand-fixed with xmlns="http://www.dataaccess.com/webservicesserver/" via curl returns the correct result (NumberToWordsResult 'one million two hundred and thirty four thousand five hundred and sixty seven'). WSDL: https://www.dataaccess.com/webservicesserver/NumberConversion.wso?WSDL (4438 bytes, WSDL 1.1, document style, empty soapAction). Fix direction: qualify the Body's payload element (and typed children) with the resolved input-element namespace from the neutral model Source.input_element '{uri}Local'; demo/demos/21-soap-adapter.sh evidently passes because loopback fixtures likely tolerate or match the unqualified shape — the demo gate does not prove live interop.
evidence: Reproduced twice at HEAD 9f193ae6 (2026-10-10, main = origin/main). --document envelope stored in tick report; curl control call succeeded. Related: error is mapped INTERNAL_ERROR for a client-side payload defect (see DF-049).
foreman_note: Tick muster-foreman-2026-10-11-04-09-07: DF-048 closed — payload root carries xmlns=<targetNamespace>. Worker code committed 50aea846 (DF-048 namespace fix only; DF-049 trimFloat fix came separately in d7e8f9a0). Live-verified against dataaccess.com NumberConversion.

title: P2: SOAP integer part serialized in scientific notation ('1.234567e+06') and fault-on-payload maps to INTERNAL_ERROR instead of BAD_REQUEST
description: Dogfood 2026-10-10 (run 14). Two secondary defects in the SOAP adapter visible from the same live test: (a) `--args '{"ubiNum": 1234567}'` with type 'integer' renders the envelope as `<ubiNum>1.234567e+06</ubiNum>` — scientific notation is not a valid xsd:integer lexical form and would be rejected by strict services even if the namespace defect (DF-048) were fixed; the XSD type table (spec PROTO-008 §3) must emit integer as a plain decimal string. (b) When the service rejects the payload, muster prints `INTERNAL_ERROR: soap: Error processing request: Invalid namespace ''` — but a bad namespace in OUR generated request is not the server failing; per spec §5 fault mapping only Server/Receiver fault codes map to INTERNAL. At minimum distinguish service-fault INTERNAL from client-side send/receive errors; exit code discipline also slips: `time` shows rc=1 but the flag-usage dump prints before the error line, burying the one-line error users need.
evidence: Envelope via `protocol soap --document`: <ubiNum>1.234567e+06</ubiNum> for JSON input 1234567; error output captured in tick report. HEAD 9f193ae6.

reasoning:
P4 — README:81-84 carries a stale and now doubly-wrong note: "the public petstore3.swagger.io demo server returns HTTP 500 on most petstore endpoints — including findByStatus AND GET /pet/1 — server-side, not a Muster bug". Measured 2026-10-18 at HEAD b5f8c1e5: GET /pet/1 returns 200 from that server, and the README's own Quick start hands the reader exactly that command 3 lines earlier (README:78 './bin/openapi-cli get-pet-by-id 1'), so the note now warns readers off a working example. The second half is wrong in the OPPOSITE direction: findByStatus DOES fail through Muster, but not server-side — Muster drops the query string from the URL, which is a code defect, not a doc one.

EVIDENCE (exact commands -> exact outputs, run 2026-10-18, HEAD b5f8c1e5):
1. Third-party server truth, hand-run:
   for p in /pet/1 /store/inventory "/pet/findByStatus?status=available" /store/order/1 "/user/login?username=u&password=p"; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3$p"; done
   -> 200, 500, 200, 404, 200. Only /store/inventory is a server-side 500; the two endpoints the note names are NOT.
2. `./bin/openapi-cli request GET https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/pet/1`
   -> {"id":1,"name":"Pet1","photoUrls":["test1","test2"],"tags":[],"status":"available"} (HTTP 200)
3. `./bin/openapi-cli generate https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/openapi.json` then `./bin/openapi-cli get-pet-by-id 1`
   -> "✓ Generated 3 command groups", then a table printing id 1 / name Pet1 / status available, stderr "HTTP response received status=\"200 OK\""
4. findByStatus through Muster vs the same URL through curl:
   `./bin/openapi-cli request GET 'https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/pet/findByStatus?status=available'`
   -> {"code":400,"message":"Input error: missing required query parameter `status`"} / Error: request failed with status 400
   same URL with curl -> HTTP 200 and a JSON array of pets.
5. Neutral repro that it is the CLI dropping the query (not the petstore mirror):
   `./bin/openapi-cli request GET 'https://postman-echo.com/get?foo=bar'`

title: P3 - audit retention is decorative: `audit info` prints 'Retention: 90 days' but NOTHING prunes or rotates the sink (no retention code anywhere in internal/audit, cmd or internal/builtin), the spec's documented default is 365, and because the sink is never pruned `audit log` re-reads and re-unmarshals the WHOLE file on every invocation (measured 11.7ms at 200 rows -> 27.1ms at 2,200 rows, strictly linear)
reasoning:
Dogfood run 20 (tick muster-dogfood-2026-10-23-12-37-51), HEAD 0bd841fe.

Claim vs code:
  `audit info` output (run20/legA-audit-chain-redaction.txt): 'Retention:        90 days' (internal/builtin/extended.go:742 prints cfg.RetentionDays; hooks.go:201 defaults it to 90).
  specs/EVENTS-AUDIT.md:13 declares RetentionDays and :25 sets the field default to 365 — read side prints 90, spec says 365.
  grep -rniE 'func .*(rotate|prune|trim|retention)|os.Truncate' --include=*.go internal/audit cmd internal/builtin | grep -v _test -> EMPTY. The only RetentionDays hits in the whole tree are the struct field, the default and that printf. So the number is reported, never enforced: an audit-enabled user's sink grows forever.

  `audit log --limit 1` on a 200-row sink   : 11.7 ms ± 0.8
  `audit log --limit 1` on a 2,200-row sink : 27.1 ms ± 1.7   (~7.7 us/row, linear)
  `audit info`          same 2,200-row sink : 23.4 ms ± 1.0

title: P3 — the documented cross-platform build path is broken on a clean tree: `./scripts/build.sh linux amd64` (specs/BUILD-SYSTEM.md:962) dies `no Go files in .../cmd`, and its LDFLAGS name the WRONG module path (anomalyco) so version stamping is silently dropped
description:
MEASURED at HEAD 8b76c62c5abf3dea2f6b0f1c18c5006ce38d6089 on the muster QA dev box (clean tree, go1.26.10 linux/amd64).

(1) THE DOCUMENTED COMMAND FAILS IMMEDIATELY. specs/BUILD-SYSTEM.md section 7.2 ('Cross-Platform Builds') documents `./scripts/build.sh linux amd64` as the build-script alternative to `make build-all`, and section 3.2 reproduces the script body as the canonical implementation.
  $ cd /home/kara/wojons/muster && bash scripts/build.sh linux amd64
  Building for linux/amd64...
  no Go files in /home/kara/wojons/muster/cmd
  rc=1
Cause: scripts/build.sh:6 sets CMD_DIR="cmd" and scripts/build.sh:39 builds `./$CMD_DIR`, but cmd/ holds only subdirectories (cmd/openapi-cli, cmd/mcp-server, cmd/daemon) and no package at its root. `ls cmd/*.go` returns nothing. The Makefile's build-all target is correct (it names each cmd/<binary> path); only this script is stale.

(2) EVEN WITH THE PATH FIXED, THE LDFLAGS ARE INERT. scripts/build.sh:14-16 stamp -X github.com/anomalyco/muster/internal/version.{Version,Commit,BuildDate}, but go.mod declares module github.com/wojons/muster, so `go build -X` targets a symbol that does not exist and Go drops it SILENTLY (no warning, rc=0). Verified as an A/B on the same tree:
  -X github.com/anomalyco/.../version.Version=v9.9.9-wrongpath  -> `openapi-cli version` prints v0.1.2-0.20261023131649-8b76c62c5abf+dirty (buildinfo fallback; the injected value is gone)
  -X github.com/wojons/.../version.Version=v9.9.9-rightpath      -> `openapi-cli version` prints v9.9.9-rightpath (injection works)
So a release built through the documented script would carry buildinfo-derived or `dev` version strings rather than the script's VERSION, and the CI 'Version guard (no binary may report dev)' invariant would not be enforced on that path.

SCOPE/SEVERITY: the main build path (`make build`, `make build-all`, CI) is unaffected, and no CI workflow or Makefile target invokes scripts/build.sh (grep: 0 hits), so this is not a red-build defect. It is a broken DOCUMENTED path plus silent version-stamp loss for anyone who follows specs/BUILD-SYSTEM.md 7.2, which is the design authority for the build system.
reasoning:
WHY A NEW ROW AND NOT A RECURRENCE: the board carries no row for scripts/build.sh at all (full-text jq over tasks.jsonl for 'build.sh' returns 0 rows). The neighbouring version-injection rows are different files/paths and are CLOSED: GAP-007 (Makefile:28 ldflags), RELEASE-002 (.goreleaser.yml ldflags), REVIEW-MUSTER-2 (`go install`/manual builds). None of them covers scripts/build.sh, and this run's A/B shows the specific consequence here (silent no-op, not an error).

WHY IT IS CLEAN-MACHINE BRITTLENESS: a fresh clone has no bin/ and no build cache; the only instruction a new contributor or a packager following section 7.2 has is this command, and it fails before compiling anything. It fails identically on the agent image (this run's fresh-install leg builds the tree fine, so the failure is the script, not the environment).

SEVERITY P3: no runtime/data impact, main build path intact; it is a documented-path break plus a silent metadata loss that would ship wrong version strings if used for a release.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `cd <repo> && bash scripts/build.sh linux amd64` exits 0 on a clean tree at the fix commit and leaves an executable at bin/muster-linux-amd64 (currently rc=1 'no Go files in <repo>/cmd').
2. The script builds the three real entry points by their actual paths (cmd/openapi-cli, cmd/mcp-server, cmd/daemon) - or is deleted and specs/BUILD-SYSTEM.md 7.2/3.2 no longer document it. A fix that silently keeps `./cmd` as the build target does not satisfy this criterion.
3. Every module path in the script's LDFLAGS matches go.mod's module (github.com/wojons/muster); `grep -c 'anomalyco' scripts/build.sh` returns 0.
4. Injection is proven, not assumed: a binary built by the script reports the script's VERSION (e.g. `VERSION=v9.9.9 bash scripts/build.sh linux amd64 && ./bin/muster-linux-amd64 version` contains v9.9.9), not a buildinfo fallback and not `dev`.
5. specs/BUILD-SYSTEM.md section 7.2's command list and section 3.2's embedded script body match the shipped script byte-for-byte in the flags/paths they claim (a reader following the spec reaches a working build).

Integer performance may suffer.` followed by `v0.0.0-20261023193045-0a70dffdc0db (0a70dffdc0db)`.

REPRODUCED OFF-BATTERY (dev box, go1.26.10, no battery involved), first at HEAD 8b76c62c and re-verified at HEAD 7cb5f306 with a CLI rebuilt from that tree:
  1. `( ulimit -v 3145728; ./openapi-cli version ) 2>err.txt >out.txt` -> rc=0, out.txt `v0.1.2-0.20261023200124-7cb5f3066e65+dirty (7cb5f3066e65-dirty)`, err.txt `2026/10/23 15:06:31 Starlark failed to allocate 4GB address space: cannot allocate memory. Integer performance may suffer.` Uncapped, the SAME binary writes NOTHING to stderr.
  2. `( ulimit -v 3145728; go test -short -count=1 -run TestCLI_VersionCommand ./test/e2e/ )` -> FAIL at cli_test.go:30 with the identical message (deterministic, 0.01s).

The warning is emitted by the LIBRARY, not by a muster log call, so no `--quiet`/`--json` flag can suppress it and it lands on stderr for every subcommand (version, dsl, request, mcp proxy) in any address-space-capped environment.

BLAST RADIUS: (a) user-facing stderr noise on every command in ulimit -v sandboxes, terminal jails, and RLIMIT_AS-capped CI runners; wrappers that treat stderr as failure trip on it; (b) the repo's own e2e gate is red under a memory cap because cli_test.go:22-33 uses `cmd.CombinedOutput()` and asserts the WHOLE combined blob matches a single-line regex, so any unrelated stderr line fails the assertion.

Today `( ulimit -v 3145728; go test -short -count=1 ./pkg/dsl/ )` is green while test/e2e is red for the same cap on the same host - same root cause, second surface, so this is filed as a recurrence (--recur QA-MUSTER-8) rather than a fresh base id.

This is a product defect, not a harness limitation: the failing assertion is exercised by the repo's own test with the repo's own documented cap, and the stderr pollution is produced by product code paths (any command) in an environment the project explicitly tests (chaos-resource cell cap=3145728KB).

title: P2 - `openapi-daemon stop|restart` reports 'daemon (PID N) did not exit after SIGTERM' inside any container whose PID 1 does not reap: the stopped daemon becomes a ZOMBIE and isProcessRunning() counts a zombie as alive, so the repo's CI (act) leg is deterministically red on TestBinaryExecution_RestartCommand
description:
MEASURED. Battery tick muster-qa-2026-10-23-19-22-39 (agent c510dd7e @ bunker-mvp, HEAD 8b76c62c) graded ci-pass FAIL: the act leg's `Test` step failed after 1m41s but `act -q` elides per-step stdout, so ci.log names no failing test (harness observability gap, recorded separately). Re-running the CI-exact command off-battery in the SAME image the battery uses - `catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest`, go1.26.10, `go test -short -count=1 $(go list ./... | grep -v -e test/stability -e test/security)` - produced EXACTLY ONE red package out of 59: `--- FAIL: TestBinaryExecution_RestartCommand (6.23s)` / `cmd/daemon/integration_test.go:209` / `command [restart --socket-path /tmp/mdtsock.../test-restart.sock] failed: Error: daemon (PID 13304) did not exit after SIGTERM`.

DETERMINISM A/B (same HEAD 8b76c62c, same go1.26.10, only the execution environment differs):
  - act container image, 2/2 FAIL (5.89s, 5.54s), re-run at HEAD 2507d70c: FAIL (5.59s)
  - dev box, 2/2 PASS (1.39s, 1.15s), re-run at HEAD 2507d70c: PASS (0.695s)

MECHANISM PROVEN IN A CONTAINER, not inferred. act's container entrypoint is `tail -f /dev/null` (ci.log: `docker create image=catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest ... entrypoint=["tail" "-f" "/dev/null"]`); tail never reaps children. Reproduced exactly: `docker run -d --entrypoint tail catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest -f /dev/null`, then `docker exec` a freshly built `openapi-daemon start --socket-path /tmp/z2.sock` followed by `kill -TERM <pid>`:
    PID1=tail
    ps -o pid,ppid,stat -p <pid>  ->  <pid>  1  Zs  [od] <defunct>
The daemon exited, but it is a zombie reparented to PID 1. `cmd/daemon/main.go:481-491` sends SIGTERM, waits up to 5s calling `isProcessRunning(pid)`, and `cmd/daemon/pidfile_unix.go:49-50` defines 'running' as `proc.Signal(syscall.Signal(0)) == nil` - which is TRUE for a zombie, forever. The same predicate backs the `stop` subcommand (`cmd/daemon/main.go:255-290`, `internal/builtin/daemon.go:246`), so stop/restart report failure on a daemon that did stop.

USER IMPACT: the documented docker deployment path is affected - any container whose entrypoint is the app's own shell (plain `docker run`, act, k8s pods without an init/reaper) gets `openapi-daemon restart` exiting 1 with a misleading 'did not exit after SIGTERM', while `status`/`start` behave normally. The product's own CI gate cannot go green in a container for the same reason.
reasoning:
Graded a PRODUCT defect rather than harness brittleness because (a) the failure is produced by product code - the liveness predicate in cmd/daemon/pidfile_unix.go treats a defunct process as running - not by the test harness; (b) it reproduces with the repository's own binary and its own container image, with no battery involvement, on two independent hosts; (c) the dev-box arm passes at the same HEAD and the same Go version, so this is not a toolchain or load artefact; (d) the test asserts a user-facing CLI outcome (`restart` must succeed), and the contract is stated in the test's own comments ('Restart: stops the old daemon and spawns a fresh one on the same socket', integration_test.go:220-225).

WHY NO ROW EXISTED: hosted GitHub Actions is zero-step red on an org billing block (open rows CI-BILLING-002/003, INT-CI-001, REVIEW2-MUSTER-5), so this container-only failure has never been visible from CI runs; it only shows up when the act leg is actually executed, which the battery does. Deduped against the board: no open row mentions TestBinaryExecution_RestartCommand, zombie/defunct liveness, or SIGTERM on restart.

HARNESS NOTE (separate, no product row): the act leg's step output is not captured (`act -q`), so a red act leg cannot name its own failing test; that is why the battery ci-pass cell says only 'act leg rc=1'. The generator should drop `-q` for the Test step (or tee step logs) so future act reds are self-explaining.
acceptance_criteria: 1. In a container whose PID 1 does not reap - `docker run -d --entrypoint tail catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest -f /dev/null` then `docker exec` - `go test -short -count=1 -run TestBinaryExecution_RestartCommand ./cmd/daemon/` exits 0; at HEAD 2507d70c the same command exits 1 with `daemon (PID N) did not exit after SIGTERM`. 2. On an ordinary dev box `go test -short -count=1 -run TestBinaryExecution_RestartCommand ./cmd/daemon/` still exits 0 (currently 0.695s PASS - must not regress). 3. The liveness predicate reports a Linux `Z` (defunct) process as NOT running (read /proc/<pid>/stat state or reap-aware equivalent), and the Windows implementation in cmd/daemon/pidfile_windows.go keeps its current behaviour; the fix cites both file:line in its foreman_note. 4. `openapi-daemon stop --socket-path <sock>` in that same non-reaping container prints the success message and exits 0 after SIGTERM - proving the fix is in the predicate, not a restart-only special case. 5. A transcript proving the zombie (`ps -o pid,ppid,stat -p <pid>` showing `Zs [od] <defunct>` with PPID 1) is captured before and after the fix and stored under .coding-hermes/qa-evidence/. 6. A re-run of the battery's ci-pass cell on a HEAD containing the fix grades OK, or the act leg's Test-step output is captured so the remaining red is nameable.
